RaMP multi-database ORA returned Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182, FDR 1.22e-15, fold enrichment 1801) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, FDR 1.22e-15; KEGG:map00052, FDR 1.22e-15) as the two top-ranked hits, with five input metabolites — galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, and glycerol — mapped to these pathways. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) as the top hit (p = 9.53e-10, 5/27 metabolites overlapping), producing a concordant cross-paradigm verdict with no namespace artefact. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis ranked Galactose metabolism fourth (p = 0.000924, 10/11 input overlap) and Starch and Sucrose Metabolism sixth (p = 0.00227), validating the same carbohydrate-active metabolic axis via an empirical-compound network approach that is blind to annotation quality. Acetylcholine (ChEBI:15355) and aflatoxin B1 exo-8,9-epoxide (ChEBI:30725) were not captured in the core galactose pathways; the epoxide appears as a Mummichog glycerophospholipid-network neighbor (rank 5) rather than a direct ORA member, consistent with its role as an exogenous electrophile engaging lipid-signalling processes rather than primary carbohydrate flux. The driver metabolite cluster (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) spans the Leloir pathway and its downstream sugar alcohol and osmolyte branches, indicating that the treatment condition imposes a systemic shift in galactose utilisation with secondary effects on glycerophospholipid metabolism via shared glycerol-3-phosphate intermediates.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-database over-representation analysis of seven differentially abundant metabolites identified galactose metabolism as the dominant disrupted pathway across all paradigms. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052) first with p = 9.533×10⁻¹⁰, and RaMP confirmed the same finding at FDR 1.22×10⁻¹⁵ across SMPDB and KEGG namespaces. Five of the seven input metabolites—galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, and glycerol—mapped to this pathway. Galactinol, the most structurally distinctive input, is a raffinose-family oligosaccharide synthesised from UDP-galactose and myo-inositol; it drives the pathway by serving as the direct galactose donor that generates galactose-1-phosphate through GALK1 catalysis. Sucrose and myo-inositol are pathway intermediates, with sucrose feeding galactose into the Leloir pathway and myo-inositol providing the inositol backbone for galactinol synthesis. Galactitol, the galactose reduction product, is a well-characterised toxic metabolite that accumulates in classic galactosemia. Glycerol, also confirmed as a pathway member in the RaMP hit list, feeds into the glycolytic arm downstream of galactose metabolism. Secondary enrichment in the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, FDR 1.29×10⁻⁴) was supported by myo-inositol and glycerol. Acetylcholine and 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 did not meet annotation thresholds in either tool and were excluded from pathway membership claims. The cross-paradigm consensus identifies Galactose Metabolism as the primary biological story, with five metabolites converging on Leloir-pathway intermediates and downstream consequences.
